Maria: Quick heads-up — after the AVX kernel switch on canary we started seeing steady memory growth in the KV cache for long chat sessions. Not sure it's pure leak; looks like paging/fragmentation + lower reuse of prefix entries. Anyone else noticed this?

Aj: saw it on the profiler too. pagefaults spike ~30s into long sessions, reuse_rate drops compared to baseline. flame graph attached (short).

Kevin: details? which kernel build/tag? could be a change in our hash canonicalization path that affects key equality on the hot path.

Maria: canary was avx2-opt-v2 (deployed ~3276543100). perf-bot reported small latency improvements but memory 90th went up. Logs: `/var/log/kv/prefetch.log` shows more page-in churn.

perf-bot: Perf CI summary: canary avx2-opt-v2 vs baseline
- p50 latency: -3%
- p95 latency: -1%
- kv_resident: +12% at 90th
- reuse_rate(prefix): baseline=0.71 -> canary=0.54

Tara: can you paste the small profiler dump? also curious if batching heuristics changed; smaller batches can reduce KV coalescing and hurt reuse.

Aj: paste of quick metric snapshot:
```
kv_cache.entries=1_210_423
kv_cache.resident_mb=982
pages_in=123_892
reuse_rate_prefix=0.54
avg_kv_growth_per_longctx_mb=4.1
hash_seed=0x9af3
```

Kevin: that hash_seed looks suspicious — we recently added a runtime-specific per-process salt in the AVX path to avoid cross-tenant collisions when using SIMD hashing. If the salt varies per worker more often, identical prefixes won't hit the same key, causing reuse to drop and memory to grow.

Maria: ah — we expected the salt to be stable per-process but AVX path may be reinitializing the rng on worker handoff. That could explain the fragmentation of entries across buckets -> more resident pages.

Tara: quick mitigation idea: make keying path fallback to the canonical (stable) salt for prefix cache only, keep randomized salt for other tables. Low risk, quick patch.

Aj: alternative: add a merge-pass in page scrubber to dedupe equivalent prefixes across shards, but that's heavier. I'd prefer the targeted key fix first.

Kevin: agreed. I'll prepare a minimal change: preserve global prefix_salt across kernel entrypoints. Also adding a metric `prefix_key_aliases` so we can measure how often identical logical keys map to distinct cache keys.

Maria: can you run a canary with that flag toggled? I'll queue a workload with long chat sessions (100 sessions, avg 5k tokens) to reproduce growth.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: kernel=avx2-opt-v2 + prefix_salt-stable flag -> start 3276543600

perf-bot: Note — make sure batching config matches baseline (batch_size distribution) for the run; otherwise reuse comparisons are noisy.

Tara: ack, I'll pin batching to baseline for the validation run.

Maria: good plan — thanks all. I'll follow up with the bisect PR and a short postmortem if the stable-salt fix regresses latency.

Kevin: ping me if you need help with the metric plumbing (I'll add `prefix_key_aliases` to statsd).

Maria: tagging @Kevin @Tara for visibility, will post results here. :thumbsup:

Tara: ack :+1:
